title: Platform operator resumption after region split and traffic reconverge
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This runbook describes operator procedures, automated safety checks, and post-incident actions for an operational scenario we call a "region split and traffic reconverge": a partial network partition or control-plane divergence that temporarily causes one or more regions to route traffic independently and then later reconverge, creating sudden blended traffic, cache hot-path conflicts, and request replay storms. The goal is to safely resume normal cross-region traffic, preserve SLOs, avoid cascading evictions, and capture accurate incident telemetry.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to any multi-region deployment where traffic is sharded by region and safe-fallback routing is enabled (hosted and dedicated clusters).
- Primary audience: platform operators, SRE oncall, and runtime owners.
- Not covered: full disaster recovery (DR) for region loss, hardware-level rack failure response—see DR runbook.

Why this matters:
- Reconverge events commonly surface as: token-cost spikes, sudden tail-latency regressions, model-variant fallback cascades, and operator confusion about which capacity pool is authoritative. Without controlled resumption, service can oversubscribe caches and GPU pools and breach customer SLOs.

Preconditions and signals (what to watch for):
- Primary alert triggers that may indicate region split or reconverge:
  - high inter-region queueing rate (metric: runtime.region_queue_rate)
  - rapid increase in cross-region retry ratio (metric: network.cross_region_retries > 5% sustained over 2m)
  - KV prefix-cache churn spike (metric: cache.kv_churn_rate > 200 ops/s)
  - burst of model-variant swaps / fallbacks (metric: serving.model_fallback_rate)
  - operator-facing dashboard: "Regional Traffic Entropy" shows >25% unexpected route shifts
- Secondary indicators: elevated GPU utilization in previously-idle pools, token-cost-per-request jump, and routing-controller leadership flaps.

Immediate operator playbook (step-by-step):
1) Triage and safe-hold:
   - Confirm alert correlation across control plane and runtime dashboards. Note timestamps and region names.
   - Engage oncall and post a short status in #platform-ops. Include affected regions, observed SLO impact, and whether automated failovers are active.
   - Issue a "traffic hold" if the routing-controller indicates unstable leader election: scale routing-controller replicas to 1 in affected region to avoid split-brain decisions. CLI: 
     - kubectl -n infra scale deployment/routing-controller --replicas=1 --context=<region-context>
2) Rate-limits and tenant credits:
   - Temporarily enable soft global rate-limit at the API edge to keep token surge under control. Recommended protection: 30% of historical peak qps.
   - If tenant-burst-credit system exists, disable auto-buydown to avoid silent overconsumption. CLI example: 
     - redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope global --max-qps <calculated-qps>
3) Stabilize caches and KV state:
   - Pause cross-region cache invalidations for 3 minutes to avoid high churn. Use admin toggle: 
     - redwood-admin cache toggles set cross_region_invalidation false --duration 3m
   - Run a focused prefix-cache reconciliation for hot prefixes observed in the churn metric. Script: 
     - scripts/prefix_reconcile.sh --prefixes <comma-separated> --regions <list>
4) Gradual reconverge:
   - Using the routing-controller, resume inter-region routing in stages: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%. Wait 90–180s between steps and validate metrics at each step. CLI: 
     - redwoodctl routing adjust --target-region <region> --weight 10
     - validate: curl -sS http://observability/api/query?metric=runtime.latency_p50&region=<region>
   - At each stage run the "mini-health-check": synthetic-sla-e2e against a representative tenant set (runbook provides list).
5) Monitor for regressions and backoff if needed:
   - If tail latency or fallback rate increases by >20% compared to pre-split baseline, immediately revert last weight step and wait 10m.
   - If model fallback spikes persist, consider directing traffic to a compatible model variant pool until full cache warmup is achieved.

Automated actions and safety nets (what should already be configured):
- Routing-controller should have staged-weighting APIs and an idempotent resume operation.
- Global soft rate-limiter that can be toggled from the console and CLI.
- Cache reconciliation job that can be invoked with prefix lists and dry-run outputs.
- Canary synthetic suite that runs within operator namespace and measures p50/p95/p99 and SLO pass rate.

Runbook CLI/automation snippets (operators will copy/paste):
- Place a traffic hold:
  - kubectl -n infra scale deployment/routing-controller --replicas=1 --context=eu-west-1
- Set global rate-limit to 60k qps:
  - redwoodctl rate-limit set --scope global --max-qps 60000 --reason "region reconverge safe-hold"
- Stage routing weight:
  - redwoodctl routing adjust --target-region eu-west-1 --weight 30 --service inference-api --note "reconverge stage 2"
- Pause cross-region invalidations: 
  - redwood-admin cache toggles set cross_region_invalidation false --duration 180s
- Run cache-reconcile dry-run: 
  - scripts/prefix_reconcile.sh --prefixes ai/sessions,ai/chat --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1 --dry-run

Dashboards and alerts to observe during reconverge:
- Regional Traffic Entropy (dashboard id: platform/entropy): single-pane view of routing weights and route flaps.
- runtime.region_queue_rate (graph): ensure queueing does not exceed 80% of configured queue depth.
- serving.model_fallback_rate: alert on >5% sustained over 5m.
- cache.kv_churn_rate: alert on >200 ops/s sustained for 2m.
- telemetry/cost_per_token_by_region: watch for sudden 10%+ delta.

SLO impact matrix (use this quick reference to communicate with stakeholders):
| SLO | Immediate safe target | When to page | Communication note |
|-----|-----------------------|--------------|--------------------|
| p99 latency (inference) | < 2.5x baseline | p99 > 3x baseline for 5m | Rebalance traffic to lower-latency region or enable degraded SLO notice |
| availability (per-tenant) | >= 99% | availability < 98% for 10m | Consider tenant-level traffic divert or rate-limiting |
| request success rate | >= 99.5% | < 99% sustained 5m | Use model-variant fallback catalog to avoid failure loops |

Post-incident recovery checklist (minimum required items):
1) Confirm all routing weights are at intended steady-state and document the final weights.
2) Re-enable automated invalidations and reconcile caches fully. Run full prefix_reconcile: scripts/prefix_reconcile.sh --prefixes all --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1 --commit
3) Release global rate-limits and re-enable tenant auto-buydown.
4) Export and attach the following artifacts to the incident ticket: routing-controller logs, cache-reconcile logs, synthetic-e2e run outputs, model-fallback traces, and any redwoodctl commands executed.
4) Create customer-facing status update draft if customer-impacting SLOs were breached. Use the template in incident-commms.

Postmortem and telemetry asks (data to collect and owners):
- Metrics to store (owner): routing-controller events (platform), cache.kv_churn_rate (eng-platform), model_fallback_rate (runtime team).
- Traces: include 10-minute windows before, during, and after reconverge for representative tenants. (owner: eng-platform observability)
- Postmortem owner: person-oncall for the incident. Deadline: initial draft in 72h, final in 10 business days.

Known failure modes and mitigations (short catalog):
- Failure mode: routing-controller leader flaps during weight stage -> mitigation: revert to last known good weight, pin leader to a single replica.
- Failure mode: cache hot-prefix storm -> mitigation: paused invalidations, targeted reconciliation, soft global rate-limit.
- Failure mode: tenant auto-buydown hides throttling -> mitigation: temporarily disable auto-buydown and notify billing/CS.

Runbook maintenance and test cadence:
- Owners must run a reconverge tabletop quarterly in the gameday schedule.
- Automated reconverge failure-injection tests added to the chaos pipeline monthly.
- This runbook is reviewed every 6 months; changes require reviewers from routing, serving-runtime, and observability teams.

Ownership and escalation path:
- Primary owner: eng-platform oncall (pager: #platform-oncall).
- Secondary escalation: runtime lead (pager: runtime-lead).
- Executive escalation: Director of Platform Engineering.

Appendix: quick-reference commands and checklists (copyable):
- Emergency resume abort: redwoodctl routing adjust --target-region <region> --weight 0 --reason "abort reconverge"
- Full cache reconcile commit: scripts/prefix_reconcile.sh --prefixes all --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1 --commit | tee /tmp/reconcile-commit.log
- Synthetic test runner: ./ci/synthetics/run_group.sh --group reconverge-sanity --output /tmp/synthetics-reconverge.json

Related pages and references:
- region-surge-prediction-and-operator-guided-failover-playbook (see predictive gating thresholds)
- regional-failure-mode-mapping-and-observability-patterns (dashboard layouts and example queries)
- cold-start-warmup-orchestration-runbook (cache warmup patterns)
